description: A Scala 3 web framework with routing, JSON and form handling, validation, and integrations for multiple HTTP servers.
rules: Use Scala 3 and choose the Sharaf server adapter module that matches the application's HTTP server.

Sharaf core already includes Tupson, sttp client4, Formson, Querson, and Validson. Reuse them before adding overlapping JSON, HTTP, parsing, or validation libraries; add an alternative only for a concrete application requirement.

Use sttp client4 for outbound HTTP calls and HTTP integration tests instead of java.net.http.HttpClient; sttp.client4.quick.* is suitable for simple synchronous JVM tests. Choose a backend supported on the target platform.
Derive FormDataRW from ba.sake.formson for typed form models; use bodyFormValidated[T] with a Validson Validator when form input needs validation.
Form support varies by adapter: Undertow supports URL-encoded and multipart; http4s and JDK support URL-encoded; Helidon and snunit do not support multipart.
Derive QueryStringRW from ba.sake.querson for typed query parameters; queryParams[T] parses but does not validate, so use queryParamsValidated[T] when validation is required.
Use queryParamsRaw for dynamic query parameters or when the raw Map[String, Seq[String]] representation is more appropriate.
Derive JsonRW from ba.sake.tupson for JSON models; read request bodies with Request.current.bodyJson[Model].
Return JSON values with Response.withBody(value), and configure ExceptionMapper.json for JSON error responses.
Use bodyJsonValidated[Model] with a derived ba.sake.validson.Validator when request fields need validation.
For derivation involving default values, enable -Yretain-trees in your build tool's Scala compiler options. This repository uses Deder; consumer applications should retain their existing build tool.
Undertow is the stable JVM adapter; http4s and JDK are beta, while Helidon and snunit are experimental. Check platform support before choosing.

Use the Sharaf server wrappers for Undertow, http4s, Helidon, JDK HttpServer, or snunit rather than recreating their request/response adapters. Start HTTP integration tests through the application's real handler composition, use MUnit, and use NetworkUtils.getFreePort() where supported; stop the server after testing.

Scala Native is supported by sharaf-core, sharaf-http4s, sharaf-snunit, sharaf-jdbc-session, Formson, Querson, and Validson. Undertow, Helidon, JDK HttpServer, sharaf-pac4j, and sharaf-hepek-components are JVM-only; Twirl response support is also JVM-only. Keep JVM APIs and dependencies out of shared and Native sources.

Querson and Validson are built for Scala.js. Sharaf core and server adapters are not Scala.js libraries; Formson's Scala.js modules are currently excluded from this repository's build because java.nio.Path is unsupported. Check deder.pkl for enabled modules and Scala/Scala.js/Scala Native versions.

Use the optional sharaf-pac4j module with Pac4jSecurityConfig, Pac4jSecurityHandler, and SecurityService for authentication and authorization. It includes pac4j-core; add the mechanism-specific pac4j-http, pac4j-jwt, pac4j-oauth, or pac4j-oidc module as needed. Reuse examples/user-pass-form, examples/jwt, examples/oauth2, and sharaf-pac4j tests instead of writing a parallel security integration.
For production authentication, use HTTPS, protect browser forms against CSRF, keep secrets out of source, and use a shared persistent session store for replicas.

Use the optional sharaf-jdbc-session module's JdbcSessionStore for JDBC-backed sessions. It uses Squery and supports JVM and Scala Native; supply a DataSource, a platform-compatible database driver, and a JVM connection pool as needed. Apply the supplied schema templates through application-owned migrations; the store does not create tables at startup. Schedule deleteExpired() for expired-row cleanup.
For stateless bearer-token APIs, follow the pac4j HeaderClient and NoOpSessionStore example; do not add browser sessions unless the authentication flow needs them.

The form-login example adds jBCrypt for password hashing. Security tests use pac4j-testkit and mock-oauth2-server; H2 and scala-native-jdbc-sqlite are test/example database choices, not mandatory production dependencies.

For JVM HTML/XML responses, reuse the included Twirl API through ba.sake.sharaf.{*, given}, html interpolation, and Response.withBody. For Hepek HtmlPage responses, add sharaf-hepek-components and import ba.sake.sharaf.hepek.given; Scalatags is a separate optional dependency as shown in examples/scala-cli/html_scalatags.sc.

For interactive server-rendered pages, follow examples/htmx and return HTML fragments. Reuse the application's htmx version and existing rendering library before adding custom JavaScript or another UI framework; htmx is a browser asset, not a Sharaf core dependency.

The Undertow adapter includes tupson-config and Typesafe Config; reuse JsonRW and parseConfig[T] for typed external configuration. Do not assume those dependencies are included by other server adapters; Helidon also has its own YAML configuration integration.

For application SQL access, follow the Squery example in docs/content/tutorials/sql.md and add the database driver and connection pool needed by the application. Squery is included by sharaf-jdbc-session, not by sharaf-core.

Squery also provides a code generator for database row models and DAOs. Prefer generated models and DAOs where they fit instead of hand-writing equivalent table mappings and CRUD; run generation against the migrated schema through the existing build integration or Squery CLI. Keep generation tooling off the application runtime classpath. See https://sake92.github.io/squery/tutorials/codegen.html.

When the user requests database migrations without specifying a migration tool, default to Flyway. Honor an explicitly requested tool or the application's established migration setup. Keep schema changes in application-owned, versioned migrations, including any Sharaf JDBC session schema; regenerate Squery models and DAOs after applying schema changes.

For OpenAPI-first applications, use OpenAPI4s at build time with the Sharaf, Tupson, and Validson backends and optionally a generated sttp client. Reuse the application's Deder, sbt, or Mill integration; do not add a second build tool or put the generator on the runtime classpath. See docs/content/tutorials/openapi.md.

Sharaf accepts geny.Writable response bodies and preserves their httpContentType when provided. Reuse this response support for existing Geny values instead of adding a custom writer. Fastparse, sourcecode, and scala-java-time serve parsing, derivation, and platform compatibility; prefer Sharaf's public parsing APIs for application input.

Reuse the application's logging setup; Deder examples add Logback explicitly. jQuery and Swagger UI WebJars are test/example or optional UI assets, not required Sharaf runtime integrations; reuse the existing static-resource handling when serving them.
Treat the JWT example's inline signing secret and printed test token as demonstration-only, never as production configuration.
Treat mutable in-memory state in tutorials as demonstration-only; use a persistent store in real applications.
